# Tapproval

> Tapproval is a remote control for Claude Code and Codex on your Apple Watch.
> Approve what your agent asks, answer its questions, follow it live and
> send it on, from your wrist. When the agent on your computer asks
> permission, the question appears on the watch, marked with one of five
> risk tiers, and one tap answers it.
> No account and no server of ours. Independent; not affiliated with Anthropic or OpenAI.
> Made for people who run Claude Code or Codex and step away while it works.
> Claude Code and Codex, side by side, since version 3.0.
> Not to be confused with tapproval.vercel.app, a separate phone-notification
> tool by another developer.

## What it does
- Approve or deny Claude Code and Codex permission prompts with one tap on the watch.
- Sorts every request into one of five risk tiers on the computer; the card
  shows the tier. Nothing is approved automatically unless the user turns
  that on, and a CRITICAL request never is.
- Shows which sessions need you, which are running and which are idle,
  grouped by what they need and named with their project; read a
  conversation and reply, or start a new session from the watch.
- One conversation, everywhere: a message sent from the watch to a session
  open on the computer goes into that session, so the terminal and the
  Claude app on the phone show it and the answer, which opens with the
  watch mark and the user's words. What is typed in the terminal or on the
  phone shows on the watch. When an instruction from the wrist needs a yes
  first, Claude asks it back as a question card on the watch.
- Replies and plans read on the watch the way they do on the phone: bold,
  lists and indented sub-points.
- Multiple-choice questions arrive with the same choices as on the desktop; several questions arrive one after another, and more than one answer can be picked where the agent allows it.

## What it needs
- An Apple Watch running watchOS 10 or later.
- Claude Code or Codex on a Mac or a Linux machine, or on Windows as a preview
  (tested on GitHub's Windows machines, not yet on a real PC). The buzz
  while the app is closed is Mac-only; elsewhere cards wait until the app
  is opened.
- Tapproval Base, the free, open-source helper (MIT licence; the
  tapproval-helper plugin and repository), which Claude Code installs
  when told: "Install the Tapproval plugin from marcobelini/tapproval-helper".
  For Codex, one command installs it:
  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marcobelini/tapproval-helper/main/install.sh | bash
  then open codex once and choose "Trust all and continue", because Codex
  runs a hook only after the user approves it.
- Works on the same Wi-Fi, or away from home through a private travel address.

## Codex (since 3.0)
- Codex sessions join the same list as Claude Code's, each marked CC or CX;
  Codex's permission questions arrive as cards marked with
  their risk; a Codex conversation can be followed live, replied to, or
  started from the watch. The helper's one install covers both agents.

## Price
- The first 100 answers are free, shared by Claude Code and Codex; then
  $5 once unlocks unlimited answers for each agent, for good. No subscription. An optional $1 tip is offered too.
- Reading sessions and the day's overview stays free.

## Common questions
- Is there a subscription? No. 100 answers free, shared by Claude Code and
  Codex, then $5 once per agent.
- Does it work with Codex? Yes, since version 3.0; one helper install covers
  both agents.
- Does it work without the iPhone? Yes. The watch reaches the computer over
  the internet on its own, through a private travel address, and on a Mac
  through the user's own iCloud.
- Does it approve anything on its own? No, unless the user turns that on
  for the harmless tiers; a CRITICAL request never.
- Is it the same as tapproval.vercel.app? No; that is a separate
  phone-notification tool by another developer, with no watch app.

## Where to get it
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/tapproval/id6805869018
- TestFlight beta, everywhere: https://testflight.apple.com/join/dW1tYBQG
- Helper source: https://github.com/marcobelini/tapproval-helper
- More apps by the same maker, including Tapmerge (GitHub pull requests
  and issues on the Apple Watch, in development): https://apps.thoughtfulsteward.org

## Privacy
Tapproval collects nothing: no accounts, no analytics, no servers of ours.
Prompts and conversations travel between the watch and the user's own
computer, encrypted on every road (watch app 2.1): over the user's own
network (TLS pinned to the computer's own certificate), through the
user's own iCloud (card details as encrypted fields), or through the
travel address when away (bodies sealed end to end, so Cloudflare cannot
read them).
